Compare Millar's selectivity models

Source: R/select_Millar_compare.R
select_Millar_compare.Rd

Compares several selection curves fitted with select_Millar to the same data by the (quasi-) Akaike information criterion corrected for small sample sizes (AICc and QAICc).

Usage

select_Millar_compare(..., c_hat = NULL, c_hat_method = "deviance")

Arguments

...

results of select_Millar (class "select_Millar") fitted to the same data, or one list of such results. The names of the arguments (or of the list) are used as model names, otherwise the curve types (rtype).

c_hat

optional; overdispersion factor. By default (NULL), it is estimated from the model with the most parameters (see Details).

c_hat_method

method to estimate c_hat: "deviance" (default; deviance / degrees of freedom) or "pearson" (Pearson chi-square statistic / degrees of freedom).

Value

A data frame with one row per model, sorted by the QAICc, with the columns model, rtype, number of parameters (npar), deviance, degrees of freedom (dof), c_hat, AICc, QAICc, and the difference to the lowest QAICc (delta).

Details

Catches of gillnet and hook experiments are often overdispersed, i.e. more variable than expected from the multinomial model of select_Millar. The QAICc accounts for this by dividing the log-likelihood by the overdispersion factor c_hat (Burnham and Anderson 2002):

QAICc = -2 logL / c_hat + 2 K + 2 K (K + 1) / (n - K - 1),

where logL is the log-likelihood of the model, K the number of parameters (plus 1 for c_hat if c_hat > 1), and n the number of observations, here the number of non-zero cells of the catch matrix (length classes x mesh sizes). The models can only be compared with the same c_hat, which is therefore estimated from the most general model (with the most parameters; if several models have the most parameters, the one with the lowest deviance) and set to 1 if it is smaller than 1. The AICc is the same criterion without overdispersion (c_hat = 1, K without the additional parameter).

The log-likelihood is the multinomial log-likelihood of the catches conditional on the total catch per length class, without constant terms. Therefore, only differences between models fitted to the same data are meaningful. The model with the lowest QAICc (delta = 0) is the best supported model; models with delta < 2 have similar support (Burnham and Anderson 2002).

References

Burnham, K. P., Anderson, D. R., 2002. Model selection and multimodel inference: a practical information-theoretic approach. 2nd edition. Springer, New York.

Millar, R. B., Holst, R., 1997. Estimation of gillnet and hook selectivity using log-linear models. ICES Journal of Marine Science: Journal du Conseil, 54(3), 471-477.

See also

select_Millar

Examples

data(gillnet)
fits <- list(
  norm.loc = select_Millar(gillnet, x0 = NULL, rtype = "norm.loc", plot = FALSE),
  norm.sca = select_Millar(gillnet, x0 = NULL, rtype = "norm.sca", plot = FALSE),
  lognorm = select_Millar(gillnet, x0 = NULL, rtype = "lognorm", plot = FALSE),
  binorm.sca = select_Millar(gillnet, x0 = c(55, 4, 65, 4, 3),
                             rtype = "binorm.sca", plot = FALSE),
  bilognorm = select_Millar(gillnet, x0 = c(4, 0.2, 4.2, 0.1, 2),
                            rtype = "bilognorm", plot = FALSE))
select_Millar_compare(fits)
#>        model      rtype npar deviance dof    c_hat     AICc    QAICc      delta
#> 1  bilognorm  bilognorm    5 545.5352  72 7.576878 22124.56 2931.706  0.0000000
#> 2 binorm.sca binorm.sca    5 550.4941  72 7.576878 22129.52 2932.361  0.6544772
#> 3    lognorm    lognorm    2 704.2809  75 7.576878 22276.67 2945.845 14.1390214
#> 4   norm.sca   norm.sca    2 772.7613  75 7.576878 22345.15 2954.883 23.1770946
#> 5   norm.loc   norm.loc    2 862.9241  75 7.576878 22435.31 2966.783 35.0768303

## AIC of a single fit (without overdispersion)
AIC(fits$lognorm)
#> [1] 22276.52
